% sporkfigure in the paper: scaling, width warning, local node names (no errors expected here;
% the error cases are generated by test_style.py). \linewidth is 469.75pt (letter, 2.54cm margins).
\documentclass{article}
\newif\ifsporkSlides \sporkSlidesfalse
\input{copied_styles/spork_style.tex}
\input{copied_styles/code_to_tex_support.tex}
\begin{document}
% A plain picture first: its node names stay usable by later plain pictures (stock TikZ).
\tikz[remember picture] \node (Plain) {PLAINPIC};

% Figure 1, scale 1: about 120mm wide, fits (no warning). Defines A, B, aliases, pics, matrix cells,
% coordinates and prefixed names, which are all forgotten at its end.
\begin{sporkfigure}
  \node (A) [draw] at (0,0) {MEASURE};
  \node (B) [draw] at (110mm,0) {B};
  \draw [spork arrow] (A) -- (B);
  \coordinate (cc) at (0,-1);
  \node [alias=Al] (Q) at (cc) {Q};
  \draw (Al) -- (B);
  \pic (pp-) at (5,-1) {code={\node (inner) {I};}};
  \begin{scope}[name prefix=p-]
    \node (X) at (8,-1) {PX};
  \end{scope}
  \matrix (m) at (3,-1) {\node (m1) {M1}; & \node (m2) {M2}; \\};
  \draw (pp-inner) -- (m1) -- (p-X);
\end{sporkfigure}

% Figure 2, scale 2: the same names again, independently; MEASURE is twice as wide; ~ 2 x 125mm wide,
% too wide (the one width warning).
\begin{sporkfigure}[scale=2, node distance=5mm]
  \node (A) [draw] at (0,0) {MEASURE};
  \node (B) [draw, right=of A, minimum width=100mm] {B};
  \draw [spork arrow] (A) -- (B);
  % `name prefix` falls back to the unprefixed name: p-X of figure 1 is forgotten, so (X) is this X.
  \node (X) at (0,-1) {X};
  \begin{scope}[name prefix=p-]
    \draw (X) -- (B);
  \end{scope}
  \node [draw, scale=0.5] at (0,-2) {HALF};   % TikZ's own scale inside the body still works
\end{sporkfigure}

% Later plain pictures keep stock behavior for plain names.
\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay] \draw (Plain) -- ++(1,0); \end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
